models.title: Standard error of an iid sample mean
models.summary: The standard error of an iid sample mean divides the population standard deviation, or its sample estimate, by the square root of sample size.

relationship.locator: Section1.3.5.2, confidence-interval formula and one-sample t-test definition
relationship.translation_notes: Both source equations are one canonical relationship with explicit scale-estimation convention. U divided by dimensionless sqrt(n) remainsU. The variance formVar(Xbar)=sigma^2/n is its square, not a separate model. Owner-PDF locator is retained on the project-derivation citation; the relationship source is the accessible corroboration.

assumptions: Source assumption: independent equal-variance observations; the population standard deviation is finite. Normality is not needed for this standard-error identity.

models.summary: The one-sample t-statistic scales the difference between observed and hypothesized means by the estimated standard error.

variables.context: One scalar population, measurement unit U, sampling design and sample size; moment convention explicitly declared

assumptions: Exact t distribution requires independent identically normal observations with positive population variance, evaluated undermu=mu0;df=n-1.
For matched-pair tests the observations are within-pair differences and pairs are independent; n counts pairs ands is the SD of their differences.
limitations: This computes the statistic only; p-values, critical values and reject/retain decisions need a separately supplied decision rule/distribution.
A test statistic is not a posterior probability of the null. Integer and pairing checks require external binding.
